title: GPU execution fingerprinting and phase-aware telemetry for scheduler decisioning
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: The scheduler currently makes capacity and kernel-selection decisions with coarse telemetry (per-stream latencies and aggregated kernel names). This obscures phase-specific performance characteristics (prefill vs decode vs attention-heavy batches) and leads to suboptimal kernel selection and wrong autoscaling triggers.

Goal: Produce a low-overhead, production-safe telemetry surface that: (1) fingerprints GPU kernel executions to correlate spans across NVTX/trace/metrics, (2) tags executions with a phase-aware cohort id (prefill/decode/attention) and workload bucketing, and (3) exposes compact per-kernel metrics for promoter dashboards and automatic scheduler policy rules.

Scope:
- Runtime: emit a stable kernel_fingerprint and exec_id per kernel launch. Kernel fingerprint = sha1(kernel_name + launch_cfg + arg_shape_summary + quant_mode_flag). Exec_id is monotonic per request and attached as span attribute.
- Phases & cohorting: add lightweight phase tags (PREFILL, DECODE, ATTENTION, KV_CACHE_HIT/MISS) at NVTX range entry. Compute cohort_id = hash(model_name + seq_len_bucket + batch_size_bucket + quant_profile). Store cohort_id as low-cardinality label.
- Metrics: expose per-kernel counters/gauges: kernel_latency_ms_bucketed (histogram), kernel_launch_count, sm_util_percent_avg, workspace_bytes, io_wait_ms. Keep metric label cardinality low (kernel_fingerprint truncated to 10 chars, cohort_id, phase). High-cardinality attributes (full fingerprint, input shapes) go to sampled traces/logs.
- Tracing: create span naming convention: ri.exec.<phase>.v1 and attach exec_id, kernel_fingerprint, cohort_id. NVTX ranges must include the same phase tag and minimal payload to avoid overhead.
- Storage & dashboards: route metrics to Prometheus/Thanos with retention 90d; sampled traces to Jaeger/Tempo; high-cardinality logs to ClickHouse for ad-hoc debugging. Provide Grafana dashboards: per-kernel heatmap (latency P50/P95/P99 by cohort), scheduler decision trace links, and a policy regression board.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime emits kernel_fingerprint and exec_id on 100% of qualifying kernel launches with <0.25% tail added latency in microbenchmarks.
- Cohort tag appears on NVTX and spans for PREFILL/DECODE/ATTENTION stages.
- Grafana heatmap shows per-kernel P95 differences between cohorts under synthetic and production loads.
- A scheduler unit test can use the new metrics to choose a lower-latency kernel variant for 90% of synthetic traces where the variant helps.

Non-goals: full-per-input shape telemetry (high cardinality), replacing existing kernel names, or changing scheduler logic in this ticket (only provide telemetry and an interface for policy rules).

Implementation notes:
- Instrumentation entry points: kernel launcher wrapper (C++), nvtx helper (C++), trace/span layer (OpenTelemetry).
- Use a compact envelope for NVTX: tag format "ri:phase=<PHASE>,cohort=<CID>,f=<FINGERPRINT_TRUNC>" to avoid long strings on device.
- Limit NVTX metadata size to 64 bytes.
- Add sampling rules: always emit metrics; sample traces at 1% for low QPS, up to 10% for flagged cohorts.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/GPU+Execution+Fingerprinting+and+Phase-Aware+Telemetry
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5892
- Benchmark dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/kernel-heatmap

Risks & mitigations:
- Cardinality blowup: mitigate by truncating fingerprints and storing full data only in sampled traces/logs.
- NVTX overhead: cap NVTX payload, add benchmarks, and disable in low-level release builds if needed.
- Compatibility with private deployments: provide toggle to disable NVTX envelope and fallback to span-only telemetry.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Avery Chen: Initial proposal posted. Focus on meetup with runtime and telemetry teams this week. Links to the design doc and prototype included.
2026-02-24 - Ravi Patel: Design review notes - agreed on fingerprint components; suggested truncation to 10 chars for labels. Action: update envelope format and add cardinality tests.

2026-03-02 - Morgan Silva: Perf bench (micro): added kernel-level harness results. Baseline latency for attention kernel: P95=12.6ms; with our NVTX envelope + fingerprint emission P95=12.7ms (+0.8%). Need to optimize serialization path.

2026-03-05 - Elena Ruiz (Observability): Reviewed metric label strategy. Requested storing full fingerprint in logs only and only using truncated hash in Prom labels. Also requested explicit schema for Prom histograms.
2026-03-09 - Ravi Patel: PR opened for runtime wrapper and nvtx helper: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5892. PTAL: added unit tests for fingerprint generation and cohort bucketing.

2026-03-11 - Security review: preliminary review ok. Note: Private deployments must be able to disable NVTX payloads. Marked security_review_required=false for now but follow up with enterprise telemetry policy.

2026-03-12 - Bench results (staging): End-to-end A/B with scheduler using telemetry produced 11.6% reduction in tail latency for decode-heavy traffic (P95), and 4.2% CPU reduction on host scheduler due to fewer fallback events. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abcd/kernel-heatmap?view=abtest-142579
